c.tagline: Marble streets and ancient walls guard the Adriatic's jewel.

taxi.fareNote: City rides are metered; airport and long-distance transfers are typically quoted as fixed prices in advance.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide general emergency number and works for all services; 192 is police-specific, 194 is ambulance-specific.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town crowds in season; otherwise very safe

hood_desc: Historic walled city of marble streets, Baroque churches, and the famous city walls; ideal for first-timers who want to be steps from every sight, though it's pricey, car-free, and crowded midday.

Leafy pedestrian peninsula with a palm-lined promenade and pebble beaches, packed with mid-range hotels and restaurants; suits travelers wanting a relaxed, walkable base with easy bus links to Old Town.
Resort-heavy northern tip of the Lapad peninsula with large hotel complexes, pine parks, and quieter beaches; good for families and all-inclusive-style stays a short bus ride from the sights.
Upscale district just east of the walls with luxury hotels, Banje Beach, and Old Town skyline views; ideal for travelers wanting walking-distance convenience without staying inside the crowded walls.
Working port district around the ferry terminal and market halls; practical and budget-friendly for ferry travelers, but less scenic and farther from the main sights.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink throughout Croatia.

transit.pay: Buy a single-ride ticket from the driver (cash, pricier) or a cheaper prepaid ticket from kiosks/newsstands before boarding; the mCity/Libertas mobile app also sells tickets. Fares are flat regardless of distance within the city zone, and there is no integrated smart card.
transit.hours: Main lines run roughly 5am-1am with reduced frequency late at night; no true 24-hour service.
transit.note: No metro, tram, or train; Old Town itself is entirely pedestrian and closed to cars, so buses ring the walls rather than enter them.

bus: Intercity/international coaches from the Dubrovnik Bus Station (Autobusni kolodvor Dubrovnik) to Split, Zagreb, and neighboring countries
ferry: Jadrolinija coastal ferries to Split, Rijeka, and Bari (Italy)
Local ferries/catamarans to Lokrum, the Elaphiti Islands, and Korčula/Mljet

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus (Platanus/Atlas, ~30 min, timed to flights)
Local bus line 11 to Old Town (~40 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving about 10% for good service is appreciated, especially in tourist-oriented restaurants.

landmarks: City Walls of Dubrovnik
These massive medieval fortifications encircling the Old Town offer a spectacular two-kilometer walk with panoramic Adriatic views, making them Dubrovnik's most iconic attraction.
Stradun
The gleaming limestone main street of the Old Town is lined with baroque buildings, cafes, and bustling crowds, forming the pulsing heart of Dubrovnik.
Fort Lovrijenac
Perched dramatically on a cliff outside the western walls, this imposing fortress inspired King's Landing in Game of Thrones and offers unforgettable sea views.
Rector's Palace
This elegant Gothic-Renaissance palace once housed the rulers of the Republic of Ragusa and now displays historic artifacts in its atmospheric courtyard and halls.
Dubrovnik Cathedral (Cathedral of the Assumption)
This baroque cathedral houses a treasury of relics and artwork, including a reputed fragment of the True Cross, drawing visitors into its ornate interior.
Sponza Palace
A beautifully preserved Renaissance-Gothic building that once served as a customs house, now home to the city archives and a moving memorial to war victims.
Franciscan Monastery and Museum
Home to one of the world's oldest working pharmacies, this tranquil monastery features a stunning cloister and centuries of medical and religious history.
Minčeta Tower
The highest point of the city walls, this round Gothic tower provides Dubrovnik's most celebrated photo vantage point over the terracotta rooftops below.
Lokrum Island
A lush, near-mythical island just a short boat ride from the harbor, famed for its botanical garden, peacocks, and a small saltwater lake called the Dead Sea.
Dubrovnik Cable Car (Mount Srđ)
This scenic cable car whisks visitors up Mount Srđ in minutes, delivering one of the most breathtaking bird's-eye views of the walled Old Town and coastline.

train.note: Dubrovnik has no railway at all. The nearest practical station is Split — about 4 hours by frequent coach or seasonal fast catamaran — with direct trains to Zagreb and international connections from there.

bus.note: Direct coaches also reach Budva, Herceg Novi, Bar and Podgorica in Montenegro. All long-distance buses use the main station at Gruž harbour — live timetables at autobusni-kolodvor-dubrovnik.com/en.

ferry.note: The Bari car ferry (7–8h crossing) sails late March to late October, up to three times weekly in summer. Domestic catamarans: TP Line (tp-line.hr) to Korčula, Hvar and Split daily in season, plus Kapetan Luka (krilo.hr) fast boats on the same coast.
